description: The Pan-African Seaports Database describes 161 seaports in Africa and their physical characteristics, derived from satellite imagery. For each port it records the construction date, coastline orientation, shore-normal breakwater length, longshore wave power, presence of nearby sediment sources and sinks, sheltering setting, presence of coastal protection structures and changes of the adjacent beaches. It was compiled by Wiebe de Boer, Yongjing Mao, Gerben Hagenaars, Sierd de Vries, Jill Slinger and Tiedo Vellinga and published on 4TU.ResearchData in May 2019. Coverage is continental (Africa). The data are free under CC BY 4.0 as a CSV table with parameter descriptions and a KML file of port locations. Caveats: it is a one-off research compilation from imagery, and it describes coastal setting, not port capacity or traffic. The database supports exposure analysis of African ports to coastal hazards and sea level rise, studies of port impacts on shoreline change and adaptation planning. It complements the African development corridors database catalogued here.
